headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of new grid infrastructure to large energy users, primarily data centers, to reduce the financial burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer groups, ratepayer advocates, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Legislation Directing Regulators to Assign Electricity Costs to Data Centers
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation that directs regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, aiming to prevent residential customers from paying for data center generation and distribution costs. The bill addresses ballooning capacity market costs that have contributed to increases in all customers' bills due to data center demand.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency regarding the industry's water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water resource planners.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden and potential for future regulation).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Be Made Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, which will be aggregated and made available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This legislation aims to provide better data for water supply planning, especially during droughts, and address concerns about the industry's significant water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents, environmental and conservation groups, historic preservation advocates.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law Requires Noise Studies, Disclosures
news_summary: A new Virginia law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise impacts on homes and schools within 500 feet and utilities to disclose substation information. While it mandates studies and disclosures, the law does not set specific noise limits or water caps.
